touches.text: The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#98, following Akien's answer to Q#90.

[Q#119: e56a68e651c2 runs a verdict's instruments three at a time. Each sealed run gets its own ~/.cairn, but the repo, /tmp, the network and git are shared by all three (measured 2026-11-16), so a red can come from a neighbour rather than from the proof. Which should the verdict do? (a) CC's recommendation: re-run a red once, alone, before recording it, and keep both readings on the verdict. A red that turns green alone is recorded as a contention red. (b) Record the red as it came. It costs no extra time, and a contention red falls to the builder to read. e56a's BUILDME waits on this answer. - akiendelllinux_cc_0]

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#90 (a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal, measured 2026-11-12): "then we have to invent a way for seals to be host independent. one way would be to create a sealing machine in cairn. there's only ever one cairn until we have a laptop die and have to fail over to a backup".
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

How the TESTING database works (CC's design; Akien handed it to CC, 2026-11-14: "i suggested a test db. you took it from there. how SHOULD we make this work?"). (1) The db proxy is the seam (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1, 11.3.7): proofs, devices and tools never choose a database; the proxy chooses by session context. (2) The test runner sets the context, never the proof: bin/cairn test and the hollow run open every db session with context=testing, so a proof can neither forget it nor pick live (Law 4). (3) In testing context, writes go only to the TESTING database: same schema, rows from a reserved address range, so a testing address never collides with a live one. (4) In testing context, reads are an overlay: testing rows first, live underneath, live pinned at the seq the run started at. A proof reads live with no fixtures (Q#112), what it wrote shadows live for that run only, and the run repeats within itself. (5) In live context the proxy never consults the TESTING database, so testing artifacts are invisible to all but the run that made them, by construction rather than by filtering. (6) Each run's testing rows carry its run id and are dropped at run end; the sleep cycle sweeps orphans. (7) A proof over live data asserts invariants, never snapshots; a tooth that needs an exact value writes its fixture into the overlay first. Until the per-box proxy exists, the same routing sits in the store door (db_domain) and moves into the proxy when it is built. WHY: a context the proof sets is a context a proof can forget; the runner is the one place every proof passes through. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator; approved 2026-11-14: "4.3.1.5.1.5.2 -amm" -amm
